description.text:
This protocol lets clients obtain a stable uuid for each output,
identifying the physical output device behind it. The uuid is an
opaque, non-empty UTF-8 string that remains stable across sessions
and output reconnections, so clients and the compositor can persist
per-output settings and restore them after a restart.

Uuids are fixed-length, exactly 36 bytes, and never contain the
NUL byte; the canonical form is a lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal
string with hyphens, for example
8dd6d52e-1f60-4649-9c2c-6fb7e055272e.

The uuid is unique among the currently connected outputs: the
compositor must ensure that no two connected outputs report the
same uuid at the same time. The compositor assigns the uuid to each
physical output device and persists the assignment, so a given
device keeps the same uuid across sessions and across being
disconnected and reconnected. Once assigned, the uuid never changes
for the lifetime of the physical output device. Clients must not
assume the uuid is derived from any particular device attribute.

Clients obtain a uuid for a wl_output object via get_uuid on this
protocol, or for a zwlr_output_head_v1 via the companion
treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol; both entry points
return the same uuid for the same physical output device. The head
variant can identify an output that is disabled and has no live
wl_output global.

Clients must treat the uuid as opaque: they must not parse it,
derive meaning from its contents, or present it to users.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

A singleton global that creates treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects
from wl_output objects. The client calls get_uuid for each output
it wants to identify; the compositor reports the uuid in the
initial uuid event on the returned object. Multiple uuid objects
may be created for the same output; each reports independently.
description.summary: factory for output uuid objects from wl_output

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1 object and
release the client's binding to the manager global.

Existing treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects created through
this manager are not affected and must be destroyed
separately by the client.

Create a treeland_output_uuid_v1 object for the given
wl_output. The output may be in any state, including disabled:
the uuid identifies the physical device regardless of its
enabled state.

For an output that is currently disabled and has no live
wl_output global, the client should use the companion
treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol with the
corresponding zwlr_output_head_v1 instead.
description.summary: create a uuid object for a wl_output

description.text:
Represents the uuid identity of the output it was created for,
obtained from treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1.get_uuid or from
the companion treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol.
The compositor emits the uuid event once immediately after the
object is created. The uuid never changes, so the event is not
emitted again while the object exists.

The object is not tied to the lifetime of the wl_output global:
when the output is unplugged and its wl_output global is
destroyed, this object remains valid and the last reported uuid
remains the identity of the physical device, which may
reappear later with the same uuid. The client should destroy
this object when it no longer needs the mapping.

Note, because treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects are created from
multiple independent factory interfaces —
treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1 on this protocol and
treeland_output_uuid_head_manager_v1 on the companion
treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol — the
treeland_output_uuid_v1 interface is frozen at version 1.

Destroy this object. Only this object is affected; the uuid
of the output and other uuid objects for the same output
are unchanged.

Reports the current uuid of the output. It is emitted once
immediately after the object is created and never again,
because the uuid never changes for the lifetime of the
output device.

args.name: uuid
args.summary: opaque uuid identifying the physical output
